questions.stem: Why is interphase sometimes mistakenly called a 'resting phase'?

options.text: Because the cell is completely inactive during interphase
Because the cell is not dividing, even though it is actively growing and replicating DNA
Because no chemical reactions occur in the cell
Because the chromosomes are resting in the nucleus

questions.explanation: Interphase is sometimes wrongly called a resting phase because the cell is not visibly dividing. In reality, the cell is extremely active during interphase - it grows, produces proteins, replicates organelles, and copies all of its DNA.
